<STRUCT_0002> Vistoli:
<EMPHOPEN_0001>Notes on Grothendieck topologies, fibered categories and descent theory<EMPHCLOSE_0001>
<REF_0001>
<STRUCT_0003>
Contains useful facts on fibered categories, stacks and descent theory in the
fpqc topology as well as rigorous proofs.
<STRUCT_0004>
<STRUCT_0005> Knutson: <EMPHOPEN_0002>Algebraic Spaces<EMPHCLOSE_0002> <REF_0002>
<STRUCT_0006>
This book, which evolved from his PhD thesis under Michael Artin,
contains the foundations of the theory of algebraic spaces. The book
<REF_0003> frequently references this text. See also Artin's papers on
algebraic spaces: <REF_0004>,

<STRUCT_0007>
<STRUCT_0008> Grothendieck et al, <EMPHOPEN_0003>Th<ACCENT_0001>orie des Topos et Cohomologie <ACCENT_0002>tale des
Sch<ACCENT_0003>mas I, II, III<EMPHCLOSE_0003> also known as SGA4 <REF_0012>
<STRUCT_0009>
Volume 1 contains many general facts on universes, sites and fibered
categories. The word ``champ'' (French for ``stack'') appears in
Deligne's Expos<ACCENT_0004> XVIII.
<STRUCT_0010>
<STRUCT_0011> Jean Giraud: <EMPHOPEN_0004>Cohomologie non ab<ACCENT_0005>lienne<EMPHCLOSE_0004> <REF_0013>
<STRUCT_0012>
The book discusses fibered categories, stacks, torsors and gerbes over general
sites but does not discuss algebraic stacks. For instance, if <MATH_0001> is a sheaf
of abelian groups on <MATH_0002>, then in the same way <MATH_0003> can be identified
with <MATH_0004>-torsors, <MATH_0005> can be identified with an appropriately defined
set of <MATH_0006>-gerbes. When <MATH_0007> is not abelian, then <MATH_0008> is defined as the
set of <MATH_0009>-gerbes.
<STRUCT_0013>
<STRUCT_0014> Kelly and Street: <EMPHOPEN_0005>Review of the elements of 2-categories<EMPHCLOSE_0005>
<REF_0014>
<STRUCT_0015>
The category of stacks form a 2-category although a simple type of 2-category
where are 2-morphisms are invertible. This is a reference on general
2-categories. I have never used this so I cannot say how useful it is. Also
note that <REF_0015> contains some basics on 2-categories.
